hints: Children connected by wishes must make the same choice.
Each connected component contributes either all its children or none.
Use a bitset subset-sum, grouping equal component sizes.
analogy: Treat every connected group as one indivisible package whose weight is its number of children.
example: With component sizes 4 and 1, possible positive zoo counts are 1, 4 and 5, so the output is 10011.
algorithm: Find connected components using DFS or DSU, and count how many have each size. Maintain a bitset with bit 0 set. For each size s with frequency f, split f into binary-sized groups; for each group of g components, update bits |= bits << (g*s), truncating beyond n. Print bits 1 through n.
correctness: Every wish forces its endpoints, and therefore their entire connected component, to choose the same attraction. Conversely, each component can choose independently. Binary groups represent every number from 0 through f of equal-sized components, and the shifted bitset adds precisely the new attainable totals.
complexity: For n children and m wishes, components take O(n+m) time. If B grouped sizes are processed using machine words of w bits, subset-sum takes O(B*n/w) word operations and O(n) bits; B is O(sqrt(n) log n).
